road-grand-tour-of-switzerland.summary: Switzerland's signed scenic driving route: 1,643 km linking twelve UNESCO sites, five alpine passes and twenty-two lakes. It is a marked touring route rather than a single road, so you meet it in pieces - the piece here follows the Seestrasse along the eastern shore of Lake Zurich through Küsnacht, Meilen and Stäfa before turning inland.
road-grand-tour-of-switzerland.source: built from the road itself, as recorded in the scenic atlas

scenicChapters.title: Grand Tour of Switzerland
scenicChapters.narrative: Water arrives beside the road and stays for 19 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go — slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did.

scenicChapters.title: Grand Tour of Switzerland
scenicChapters.narrative: For 28 km this is Grand Tour of Switzerland, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it. Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

road-grand-tour-of-switzerland.story: 1066 km round from Zürich - plan on about 17 h 46 of riding. On the way it passes Schaffhausen, Bodensee, St. Gallen and Appenzell. The highest point is about 2,450 m. Fluela Pass is subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. It crosses Switzerland, Liechtenstein and Italy - carry ID and check vignette or toll rules. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.

scenicChapters.title: Route des Grandes Alpes
scenicChapters.narrative: The ground tilts up and stays tilted for 38 km. 1172 m of it, taken steadily rather than in one wall. A steady rhythm suits this better than bursts. The height arrives whether you hurry or not.

scenicChapters.title: Col des Gets → Col des Aravis
scenicChapters.narrative: This is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else. 49 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it.

scenicChapters.title: Route des Grandes Alpes
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 1967 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance — cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

route-des-grandes-alpes-thonon-les-bains.story: A 121 km one-way ride from near Thonon-les-Bains, about 1 h 57 of riding. The stops in between: Col des Gets and Col des Aravis. The highest point is about 1,950 m. Cormet de Roselend is subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.
